Chapter 3: Silenced by Shame—Abuse, Secrecy, and the Struggle to Be Heard.
Imagine living in a world where silence is prized above all else, and obedience isn’t just expected—it’s demanded. In a place like that, speaking up can feel not just risky, but downright impossible.
For the older sister, stepping into the Amish community didn’t bring an end to the abuse she faced at home. If anything, it just made everything more hidden, tangled up in the expectations of faith and family.
Her stepfather’s behavior only grew more disturbing. He used his role, both in the family and in the community, as a shield to intimidate and control. The older sister—now turning into a young woman—could feel his threatening presence everywhere. He always managed to find moments alone with her, touching her in ways that made her skin crawl. She’d try to keep busy, stretching out chores as long as she could, but he always found a way.
When she finally built up the courage to share what was happening, her mother wouldn’t believe her. Instead, her mom accused her of lying—of wanting to tear the family apart. Even when she reached out to community leaders, hoping for support, she was dismissed. They told her she must be confused... that things like this couldn’t possibly happen among the faithful. Their advice? Pray. Forgive. And above all, keep quiet.
Can you imagine how heavy that kind of disbelief feels? It’s absolutely crushing. The older sister started to doubt herself. Was she making this up? Was she the problem? Day by day, the shame only got heavier. She felt dirty. She felt unworthy. Most of all, she felt completely alone.
It’s easy to underestimate just how powerful shame can be. It has a way of silencing people, making them feel like they’re somehow responsible for their own pain. So, the older sister learned to keep her suffering hidden—smiling when expected, pretending everything was fine. But inside, she was falling apart.
The abuse didn’t stop. Sometimes it got worse, sometimes it faded into the background—but it never really went away. Her stepfather grew bolder, convinced that no one would ever believe her. And her mother? Her anger only grew, each punishment harsher than the last. The older sister did everything she could to protect her younger sibling, but most days, she just felt powerless.
There were times she thought about running away. But where would she go? Who would believe her? She’d been taught that the outside world was dangerous, that leaving would mean losing everything—even her soul. The unknown was terrifying, almost as frightening as staying put.
Even so, deep down, the older sister couldn’t completely silence her need for justice. Secretly, she started writing down what was happening, keeping a hidden notebook as a record. It was her quiet hope that maybe, someday, someone would listen. That the truth would finally come out.
But for now, she just kept going—doing the chores, saying her prayers, putting on a brave face—while carrying a secret that threatened to destroy her from the inside out. The silence was suffocating, but for her, it felt like the only way to survive.
